newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PM'S RIVAL ZEMAN TOPS KLAUS AGAIN IN SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PM'S RIVAL ZEMAN TOPS KLAUS AGAIN IN SURVEY.

text.p: Czech opposition leader Milos Zeman has maintained his lead in popularity over Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus amid a drop in confidence in several members of the cabinet, according to a survey released on Tuesday.

The survey, conducted in early September by the independent agency STEM showed the approval rating for Klaus, the monetarist prime minister and leader of the senior Civic Democratic Party (ODS), fell to 50 percent from 52 in May.
Klaus's key political rival, the Social Democrat (CSSD) leader and parliamentary chairman Zeman, scored a 56 percent approval rating, down from 58 percent in the previous poll.
The most popular Czech politician remains Trade and Industry Minister Vladmir Dlouhy of the junior coalition partner, the Civic Democratic Aliance (ODA), with 74 percent approval, up from 72.

STEM said last week that according to the same survey in early September, the CSSD for the first time overtook ODS in voting preference, when it received 26.3 percent and ODS 26.2 percent, two months before the Senate elections.
On Tuesday, in detailing its poll of 1,469 adult Czechs, STEM said Klaus's top party colleagues mostly had lower approval ratings than before the elections to the lower house of parliament in June.
Approval for ODS's Interior Minister Jan Ruml declined 13 percentage points to 33 percent, while that for Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik (ODS) lost nine points to 43 percent.

The survey was taken before last week's central bank forced administration of an illiquid Agrobanka a.s., the largest wholly-private bank in the country, a move which sparked the opposition's so-far unanswered calls for Kocarnik's removal.

Menwhile Petra Buzkova, vice-chairwoman of parliament and a senior CSSD member had approval of 61 percent, up from 58 percent in May, and Stanislav Gross, the leader of the party's parliamentary caucus, gained seven points to 47 percent.
Dlouhy was followed by Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec of ODS with 69 percent, up from 65, with Buzkova third and Zeman fourth.
Jan Kalvoda, ODA chiarman and justice minister lost two points and is fifth with 55 percent.
The chairman of the other junior ruling coalition partner, Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL) and agriculture minisiter Josef Lux also lost two points and is the sixth with 52 percent.
Klaus was the only other politician to top a 50 percent approval rating in the poll.

In the June parliamentary elections, the ruling three-party coalition lost its large majority in parliament, due to a stronger-than-expected second place showing by the Social Democrats in a the proportionally-based vote.
But the Senate elections, in two rounds in mid-November appear hard to judge, since they will be contested among individual candidates in 81 contituencies.
